      (1) THE AREA OF CONVECTION (INVEST 96S) PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 
0.8S 91.7E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 5.6S 90.2E, APPROXIMATELY 566 NM

DEPICTS PERSISTENT DEEP CONVECTION BUILDING OVER THE CENTER. A 171521Z 
ASCAT-B PASS SHOWS NEAR GALE-FORCE WINDS ALONG THE SOUTHERN PERIPHERY 
OF THE LOW-LEVEL CIRCULATION CENTER (LLCC). ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS 
REVEALS A MARGINAL ENVIRONMENT FOR DEVELOPMENT WITH MODERATE TO HIGH 
VERTICAL WIND SHEAR (VWS) OF (20 TO 25 KNOTS), GOOD POLEWARD UPPER-
LEVEL OUTFLOW, AND WARM SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES (SSTS) OF (28 TO 29 
C). WHILE GLOBAL DETERMINISTIC AND ENSEMBLE MODELS DEPICT A STEADY-
STATE INTENSITY TREND OVER THE NEXT 24-36 HOURS, ONLY A SLIGHT 
INCREASE IN ORGANIZATION IS NEEDED FOR 96S TO BECOME A SIGNIFICANT 
TROPICAL CYCLONE AS IT TRACKS SOUTH-SOUTHWESTWARD. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED 
SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 28 TO 33 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL 
PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1006 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR THE 
DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS
